name: PA-02
label: Safe D

key_factors: District's D+19 partisan lean strongly favors Democrats
Incumbent Brendan Boyle has a large financial advantage ($5.6M cash on hand vs. no reported fundraising for Arriaga)
Prediction markets price Boyle at roughly 97% to win
No general-election polls or expert ratings, but fundamentals leave little room for doubt
model.rationale: The fundamentals point overwhelmingly to Boyle: a D+19 district, a well-funded incumbent with no outside spending against him, and a challenger with no reported fundraising. Markets price this race at about 97% Democratic, consistent with a Safe D rating.
model.watch: Any unexpected incumbent scandal or retirement would be the main way this race could tighten, though the district's lean makes an upset very unlikely.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Brendan Boyle seeks another term in a Philadelphia-area district that leans Democratic by about 19 points. He enters the general election with more than $5.5 million on hand, while Republican challenger Jessica Arriaga reports no fundraising figures. No outside groups are spending against the incumbent.

No public general-election polls or expert ratings are available for this race, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals and prediction markets, which price Boyle's chances at roughly 97 percent. The combination of the seat's strong partisan lean, the incumbent's financial dominance, and the challenger's lack of visible resources makes this one of the least competitive House races on the map, with Boyle a heavy favorite for reelection.
